questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience the American collage life. Honestly to see, if it was like the movies (it was!).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: NCSU had a great website for incoming exchange studens. But you still have to research a lot of things yourself before arrival - such as the Visa process. I would also recommend reading all of the information on the website and in e-mails as early as possible. A lot of stuff before arrival, for instance housing application, has due dates.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a couple of days with orientation, where we got a lot of information. You could also always talk to a study abroad coordinator - they were very helpful. In general NCSU has a ton of different organizations and offices who are there to help you in any given situation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was a lot of information in just 2 days while also meeting all of the other exchange studens. Even though it was overwhelming, I recommend you to talk to as many of the other studens as possible and get some contact informations. The 2 days of orientation was the only time, where all of the exchange studens were together (mandatory).

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dorms and apartments.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I lived in a shared apartment with a kitchen, so I mostly cooked all of my meals. An other option was dinning halls.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is expensive to live on campus, but it is a really good opportunity to meet people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The process itself was okay. However I had to apply for classes very early (in februar, I believe). I had two weeks from the classes for my semester was published until I had to apply for classes. This was difficult because KU needed 6 weeks to process class requests (forhåndsgodkendelser for kurser).

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was contained personal questions (contact informations etc.), class requests, and financial statement.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: At the application proces you could reach out the KU.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: For me this process was long and messy. You have to take half of your credits within one field for visa purposes. Therefore it was a puzzle to find classes that did not overlap and also could be accepted by KU. However, the study abroad office at NCSU was very helpful. I was also waitlisted on a couple of classes, but ended up getting most of them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look at classes and send a request (forhåndsgodkendelse) to KU as soon as possible. Be open to other classes - you might not get all the classes you wanted.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some classes were great while others were a bit to easy and therefore boring.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I took some 200-400 level classes within my mayor. The 400 level classes were of course harder, but it was alright.
I also took a 100 level class in biology, which was too easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The final exam did not count a lot towards the final grade. Instead you get grated on a lot of assignments, smaller exams, tests, and participation throughout the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: BIT 473 (protein interactions). BIO 240 + BIO 242 (human anatomy and physiology + lab). BIO 105 + BIO 106 (Modern biology + lab). HESA 215 (advanced beginning swimming).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
BIT 473 (protein interactions) was a really interesting course. It was a very small class. The professor was great but also hard. I learned a lot in the class, but it was also time consuming. I would say it was a good course for biochem students.
BIO 240 + BIO 242 (human anatomy and physiology + lab) was also a really great course. The professor was so sweet and explained things very well.

Food DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Groceries were more expensive than I expected.
If you want to travel during Thanksgiving, I recommend booking flights as early as possible, since they become quite expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Groceries were more expensive than I expected.
Lyft and Uber was less expensive in Raleigh compared to many other cities in the US (usually $10-30).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are 100s of clubs. If you are interested just reach out to the club. You can always just try it.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are 100s of clubs. If you are interested just reach out to the club. You can always just try it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I was in a hiking club, which was very fun and a great way to see other places outside of Raleigh.
However, I did not use the clubs that much. Instead I went to a lot of different events the university was hosting. NCSU has a bunch of different instagram account that post about different events. It was a great way to do something fun in between classes (and there are almost always free stuff :)).
I also went to a lot of fitness classes at the gym - they have all from cycling and straight training to dance and yoga.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Definitely go to sport events. The atmosphere is so good, and it is really fun to experience university sports.
To be honest the city of Raleigh is not that exiting. However, they have a lot of cute events (especially in December), so I would recommend that you look fore those events on social media.
Raleigh also have some interesting museums that are all free.
I would also recommend seeing Duke's botanical garden.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
I knew a lot about american culture before hand, so it was not that big of a culture shock for me.
American people are very nice and helpfull, so if you have problems adjusting, you can always talk to someone.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
I lived with 3 americans which was a great opportunity.
I also only talked to americans in my classes. They are mostly very open and welcoming. I would recommend to just go talk to people in you classes even though it might seem intimidating.
Clubs are also a great way to meat local students, but I didn't use that as much.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You have to be more carefull walking around by night. I never experienced anything uncomfortable, but it is highly recommended that you are more aware and don't walk alone especially when dark outside.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The hospitality of American people. They are so sweet and welcoming, and if you are open and interested about their life, they will for sure also be nice to you.
The school system is quite different from what I was used to at KU. However I liked, that the work was more spread out trough out the semester. That what finals week were less stressful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Be ready to socialize with a lot of new people in the beginning. This is where you meet all of the other exchange students.
- Focus on having fun and say YES: ask other exchange students is they want to go to an event (they mostly does, because they are here for the same reason as you). Say yes, when people ask you (to a certain extent of cause).
- Use NSCU many facilities. The gym and libraries are great! They also have a lot of facilities if you need help with something or need to talk to someone.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: NA

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of sweet people - both other exchange students and americans.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Understanding the rules in American football :)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
